research_list.name: Patrimonio Autónomo Estrategias Inmobiliarias (Pei), BVC ticker PEI
research_list.market_position: Pei is a real estate investment vehicle listed on the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (BVC). The BVC published a page (bvc.com.co, dated 2026/10/26) describing Pei as the first real estate investment vehicle to trade on the variable-income market. Pei's own site describes it as the main real estate investment vehicle in Colombia, with a portfolio of more than 150 assets in more than 30 cities (pei.com.co, undated homepage). Pei's H1 2026 operating income was COP 425,880 million, up 5.3%, and its operating margin rose to 85.03%, 62 basis points higher (Valora Analitik, article 'Ingresos operacionales de Pei crecieron 5,3 % en el primer semestre de 2026', date not available; Pei press release 'Pei reporta ingresos por más de COP 425.000 millones al primer semestre de 2026', dated August 2026). Pei's Q1 2026 results were reported at more than COP 220,000 million in revenue (La República, article date not available; Pei LinkedIn post on Q1 2026 results, date not available). In the same Q1 2026 report, Net Operating Income (NOI) was COP 189,288 million, up 8.4%, and EBITDA was COP 160,707 million (Yahoo Noticias citing Valora Analitik, article date not available). Stockanalysis.com lists a market cap of 3.32T COP, down 2.0%, and trailing-twelve-month revenue of 926.00B COP, up 8.6%, with net income of 621.54B COP, up 26.1% (stockanalysis.com, date not available). On liquidity, LarrainVial was added as a second liquidity provider for Pei's participation securities, alongside Alianza Valores (pei.com.co and Valora Analitik, October 2026; exact publication day not available). Pei's portfolio is valued at more than COP 10.1 trillion, across corporate, commercial, logistics and other asset categories (Valora Analitik, date not available). Pei also sold 51% of Centro Comercial Plaza Central during Q2 2026 (Valora Analitik, date not available).
research_list.future_outlook: Growth catalysts: Pei has a binding agreement to acquire the portfolio of Terranum, which Valora Analitik values at roughly COP 2.8 to 3.0 trillion, with corporate, logistics and commercial assets (Valora Analitik, article dated after the September 22, 2026 agreement; the exact date is not available, and the September 22, 2026 date comes from the context provided). Pei projects revenue of COP 1.12 trillion for 2027 (Valora Analitik, article date not available). Headwinds and conditions: the Terranum acquisition is still subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals (Valora Analitik, 'Pei avanza en la compra del portafolio de Terranum con un acuerdo vinculante', date not available). A 2026 earnings analysis video (YouTube, date not available) said revenue growth has been below inflation in recent quarters; I did not verify this claim against a primary source, so I do not rely on it. Pei's own disclosures show revenue growth of 5.3% in H1 2026 and 6.9% in Q1 2026 (Valora Analitik and Yahoo Noticias, dates not available), both reported figures.
research_list.investment_potential: Bull case: Pei is the largest listed real estate vehicle in Colombia by the figures available. Its reported operating margins are high (85.03% in H1 2026, per Pei's August 2026 release), revenue and NOI are growing, and the Terranum acquisition would expand a portfolio already valued above COP 10 trillion. Its listing on the BVC gives local investors direct, liquid access to commercial real estate, and the addition of LarrainVial as a second liquidity provider in October 2026 is intended to improve trading access (Pei and Valora Analitik, October 2026). Bear case: Growth depends on closing the Terranum deal, which still requires regulatory approvals. Trading liquidity has needed market-maker support, which signals thin float and possible price volatility. The price data I could verify is limited: the stockanalysis.com market cap figure is undated, and I could not verify a current share price or dividend yield with a dated source. Main risk: execution risk on the Terranum acquisition, which would materially change the portfolio, its leverage and its distribution profile, and whose terms I could not fully verify. Suitability: Pei may suit investors who want listed exposure to Colombian commercial real estate and can accept low liquidity and deal-execution risk. This assessment is based on the partial data above and is not a recommendation to buy or sell. A complete investment view would need the current share price, the latest audited financial statements, and the final Terranum closing terms, none of which I could verify with a dated source.
